description: COTRN02C parity case 03 - REENTER plus DFHPF3, the back-navigation arm, and the primary exerciser of gate G40. RISK R-B, RECORDED AND NOT CORRECTED (practice B4): the prompt-mandated Java class for this program is TransactionViewController, and the program ADDS. app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:5 reads 'Function    : Add a new Transaction to TRANSACT file', and the online transaction inventory in README.md at line 224 - inside the table spanning README.md:213-231 - reads 'CT02 | COTRN02 | COTRN02C | Transaction Add', with the CT01 row immediately above it at line 223 reading 'Transaction View'. (The assignment brief cited README.md:222 for the CT02 row; the verified line in this checkout is 224, and the verified number is the one used here.) Rule R1 settles the conflict: the mandated name is honoured verbatim and every expectation in this file is taken from the source, so nothing is renamed, nothing is reconciled and no case in this folder is downgraded to a read-only view. The mirror-image half of the swap lives in parity/COTRN01C, whose program genuinely views. PROVENANCE, STATED HONESTLY (practice B12, risk R-A): every expected value here was derived STATICALLY - by reading app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl paragraph by paragraph and cross-checking it against the copybook byte layouts (app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy for the 160-byte communication area, app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:72-80 for the 58-byte CDEMO-CT02-INFO extension, app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy for the 50-byte cross-reference record and app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy for the 350-byte transaction record), against the twenty-one input items of app/cpy-bms/COTRN02.CPY, and against the real fixture rows copied from app/data/ASCII. It was NOT captured from a live COBOL run. AAP section 0.7.6 records eight independently verified blockers that make executing the 28 legacy programs impossible in this environment: no z/OS runtime, a COBOL compiler whose indexed file handler is disabled, subprogram linkage that cannot produce an executable, a copybook that will not parse, no Language Environment CEE services, no CICS emulator, EBCDIC fixtures needing binary handling, and no alternative compiler available. Twenty cases per program, field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-equals-zero gate per module all survive that substitution unchanged; only the provenance of the expected values differs. WHAT THIS CASE DRIVES: EIBCALEN is 218 - the 160-byte area plus the 58-byte extension, each summed field by field from its own copybook per practice B11, never by widening common.NavigationContext - and CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT arrives as 1, so the 88-level test at :120 is satisfied and the ELSE at :131 is taken. :132 performs RECEIVE-TRNADD-SCREEN, which is EXEC CICS RECEIVE MAP('COTRN2A') MAPSET('COTRN02') INTO(COTRN2AI) at :541-547, and all twenty-one input items arrive with it because every one of them carries FSET in app/bms/COTRN02.bms. The screen declared below is one an operator had filled in and had NOT confirmed - CONFIRMI is a single space - before backing out, which is precisely what lets this case assert that the arm discards the typed screen entirely: no send, no write, no message. :133 then evaluates EIBAID across five arms, and the source order is preserved with WHEN OTHER last (gate G30). Arm 1 is WHEN DFHENTER performing PROCESS-ENTER-KEY, and the ENTER paths are owned by the later cases in this folder. Arm 2 is WHEN DFHPF3 and is this case. Arm 3 is WHEN DFHPF4 performing CLEAR-CURRENT-SCREEN, owned by case04. Arm 4 is WHEN DFHPF5 performing COPY-LAST-TRAN-DATA, documented in case20. Arm 5 is WHEN OTHER, which sets the error flag, moves CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY into WS-MESSAGE and sends, owned by case05. THE ARM AND THE LEG IT TAKES: :137 tests CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM against SPACES OR LOW-VALUES, and this case takes the ELSE leg. The inbound CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM holds the concrete real caller COTRN00C - the transaction-list screen that navigates here, whose own CDEMO-CT00-INFO group at app/cbl/COTRN00C.cbl:64-70 is the byte-identical 58-byte layout that arrives in this program's CDEMO-CT02-INFO span, and which moves the operator's selection character into CDEMO-CT00-TRN-SEL-FLG and the chosen identifier into CDEMO-CT00-TRN-SELECTED at :150-151 before handing off (its own reject text at :200 names S as the one valid selection value, which is why S is the flag declared below). Because the field is populated, :140-141 copy it into CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM instead of substituting a menu. The value chosen for the inbound CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is therefore COTRN00C, stated explicitly here so no reader has to infer it. THE SIBLING SUB-BRANCH, RECORDED HERE RATHER THAN AS A TWENTY-FIRST FILE: the other leg of :137 reads, byte-exactly, WHEN DFHPF3 / IF CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM = SPACES OR LOW-VALUES / MOVE 'COMEN01C' TO CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM / ELSE / MOVE CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM TO CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM / END-IF / PERFORM RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN (:136-143). So when the inbound CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is spaces or LOW-VALUES, the response's nextProgram is COMEN01C instead of the caller, and the fallback is preserved exactly as written rather than tidied (practice B5). Gate G15 fixes this folder at exactly twenty files, so that leg is documented in this description and is deliberately NOT given a case21.json. THE WRITE ORDER, WHICH IS THE EASY THING TO GET WRONG (practice B8): :143 performs RETURN-TO-PREV-SCREEN at :500-511. Its first statement, :502-504, guards CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM - not CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM - against blank, and is not taken here because :140-141 has already filled it. Then :505 moves WS-TRANID into CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, :506 moves WS-PGMNAME into CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, and :507 moves ZEROS into CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT. :506 therefore OVERWRITES the very field :140-141 read, and it does so afterwards, so the two values differ and both are pinned below: CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM holds the inbound from-program COTRN00C while CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM holds COTRN02C. CDEMO-FROM-TRANID becomes CT02 and CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT becomes 0. CDEMO-TO-TRANID is never assigned on this path and passes through as CT02, and CDEMO-LAST-MAP and CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET are referenced nowhere in the program at all, so both pass through blank. The six CDEMO-CT02-INFO fields are carried forward untouched, which is what the echo below asserts. THE TRANSFER: :508-511 is EXEC CICS XCTL PROGRAM(CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) COMMAREA(CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), and gate G40 is what this case exists for - the transfer becomes the nextProgram response field, the client resolves it, and the whole 218-byte conversation state travels in the payload. There is no server-side forward, no redirect chain and no session anywhere (rule R6, gates G37 and G38; and although this IS a REENTER invocation, the arm sets no error, so the CSSETATY red and asterisk highlight does not apply and none is expected). The mapset and map are blanked by the transfer rather than left naming the screen being left, which this case records as their absence. termination is XCTL, so the EXEC CICS RETURN at :156-159 is never reached. WHAT THIS PATH DOES NOT DO: no dataset is read and none is written, so expectedWrites is empty; expectedMessages is empty because SEND-TRNADD-SCREEN is never performed and it is the only producer of WS-MESSAGE and ERRMSGO; and expectedReturnCode is 0 because COTRN02C is an online program that sets no RETURN-CODE and contains no CALL 'CEE3ABD' - stated rather than defaulted. TRANSACT is nevertheless seeded with three 350-byte rows and pinned unchanged on the FINAL_STATE channel, because 'exactly as seeded' is a positive assertion and that channel is the only thing able to make it. Row 0 is pinned twice over - byte for byte at the full declared 350 and also field by field across all fourteen spans of app/cpy/CVTRA05Y.cpy, the trailing FILLER X(20) among them, present and space-filled (gate G21); rows 1 and 2 are pinned byte for byte, which is already the strictest statement available about a record nothing touched. Gates G32 (this program contains zero GO TO), G35 (zero CALL 'CEE3ABD'), G39 (no pagination on this path) and G43 (no 9300-CHECK-CHANGE-IN-REC in this program) are not applicable and nothing here asserts them. INPUTS, BY BINDING KEY ONLY (gate G46): CCXREF is seeded from the first five rows of fixtures/cardxref.txt and TRANSACT from three inline rows, and no production data set name appears anywhere in this file. The cross-reference rows are carried RAW at 36 bytes and are deliberately NOT pre-padded: app/cpy/CVACT03Y.cpy declares 50 - XREF-CARD-NUM X(16) plus XREF-CUST-ID 9(09) plus XREF-ACCT-ID 9(11) plus FILLER X(14) - while the fixture omits the trailing FILLER, so the 36-to-50 pad has exactly one owner: the CARDXREF_FILLER_PAD_36_TO_50 normalisation declared below and applied by ParityCase.DatasetNormalisation.normaliseSeedRow (gate G16, risk R-F). CXACAIX is NOT seeded as a separate dataset - app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD defines it as ALTERNATE INDEX TO CCXREF VIA ACCOUNT KEY over the cross-reference cluster's own alternate-index PATH, so it is a second finder over one base cluster and never a second table (gate G45). No tenth fixture is introduced; the count stays at the nine of AAP section 0.4.9. The account identifier and card number on the screen below are read from the first row of the seeded window, so the screen names a pair that genuinely exists in the cross-reference this case seeds. THE DEAD DECLARATIONS, PRESERVED AND ASSERTED AS A NON-EVENT (practice B5): app/cbl/COTRN02C.cbl:40 declares WS-ACCTDAT-FILE PIC X(08) VALUE 'ACCTDAT ' and :89 copies CVACT01Y, and neither is ever used. The only DATASET operands in the whole program name WS-CXACAIX-FILE at :579, WS-CCXREF-FILE at :612 and WS-TRANSACT-FILE at :645, :676, :705 and :714 - ACCTDAT appears in none of them, which is what makes the declaration dead rather than merely quiet. ACCTDAT is therefore NOT seeded in this case and appears in no expectation in this case or in any other case in this folder, and the translated controller takes no AccountRepository in any constructor, so there is nowhere for a well-meaning completion of the migration to add an account read. Both the dead literal and the dead COPY are kept visible as constants rather than removed, because implementing or deleting either would be a behaviour change. GOVERNING PRACTICES: review_rules returns a single line, 'No user rules provided.', and that one line is the entire document - confirmed directly while authoring this file. No user rule governs it, and their absence is NOT licence to lower the bar: the enterprise practices of AAP section 0.10.2 bind instead. The ones this file turns on are B1 (no placeholder, no unimplemented expectation and no invented value anywhere in it), B3 (every reference tree under app/cbl, app/cpy, app/cpy-bms, app/bms, app/jcl, app/proc, app/csd, app/ctl, app/catlg and app/data is read-only and not one byte of any of them was touched), B4, B5, B7 (the clock is pinned to the same instant as case01, 2022-07-19T23:12:34, from which the header images CURDATE 07/19/22 and CURTIME 23:12:34 both follow), B8 (explicit binding keys, an explicitly named US-ASCII code page, an explicit per-field expectation for all twenty-two communication-area fields, and the :140-then-:506 write order encoded rather than implied), B11 and B12, together with rules R1, R5 (fixed width is the wire format, so every value below is stated at its declared width), R6 and R7 - and because COTRN02C contains zero GO TO, R7 here reduces to preserving the order of the five EVALUATE arms. The unit is reached as a CONTROLLER_POJO: parity.ParityHarness constructs transaction.TransactionViewController and calls its handler directly, with no MockMvc, no HTTP and no JobLauncher in the path (gate G51). DFHAID is IBM-supplied and absent from this repository (risk R-D), so the DFHPF3 mnemonic below is resolved through common.CicsAid, which reproduces it from IBM CICS documentation.
